questions.question_text:
An irregular quadrilateral plot of land is divided by a diagonal of $18\text{ m}$.
The perpendicular offsets on either side are $5\text{ m}$ and $8\text{ m}$.
What is the area of the plot?

options.why: Forgot to halve the base times height when finding the triangle areas ($18 \times 5 + 18 \times 8$).
Calculated only the larger triangle area ($1/2 \times 18 \times 8$) and omitted the smaller triangle.
Multiplied the diagonal by the sum of offsets and divided by 4 instead of 2.
Calculated $26 \times (8 + 11)$ without dividing by 2 for the triangle areas.
Calculated only the lower triangle area ($1/2 \times 26 \times 11$) and omitted the top triangle.
Used the larger height for both triangles: $\frac{1}{2} \times 26 \times 11 + \frac{1}{2} \times 26 \times 11 = 286\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text: A diagonal of an irregular quadrilateral field is divided into three consecutive segments of $12\text{ m}$, $16\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are $8\text{ m}$ and $14\text{ m}$. What is the area of the field?

options.why: Omitted the factor of one half: $38 \times (8 + 14) = 836\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $14\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 38 \times 14 = 266\text{ m}^2$.
Omitted the final diagonal segment of $10\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times (12 + 16) \times (8 + 14) = 308\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral commercial block has a diagonal of $24\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are $15\text{ m}$ and $9\text{ m}$. What is the area of the block?

options.why: Omitted the factor of one half: $24 \times (15 + 9) = 576\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $15\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 24 \times 15 = 180\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $9\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 24 \times 9 = 108\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral field has a diagonal of $20\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are $6\text{ m}$ and $14\text{ m}$. What is the area of the field?

options.why: Omitted the factor of one half: $20 \times (6 + 14) = 400\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $14\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 14 = 140\text{ m}^2$.
Subtracted the triangle areas instead of adding them: $140 - 60 = 80\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text: An irregular quadrilateral paddock has a diagonal of $160\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are $45\text{ m}$ and $65\text{ m}$. What is its area in square metres?

options.why: Omitted the factor of one half: $160 \times (45 + 65) = 17\,600\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $65\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 160 \times 65 = 5200\text{ m}^2$.
Subtracted the triangle areas instead of adding them: $5200 - 3600 = 1600\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text: A quadrilateral field $PQRS$ has diagonal $PR = 16\text{ m}$. The perpendicular offsets from $Q$ and $S$ meet $PR$ at the same point, $6\text{ m}$ from $P$ and $10\text{ m}$ from $R$. The offsets are $8\text{ m}$ and $5\text{ m}$ respectively, on opposite sides of $PR$. What is the perimeter to the nearest metre?

options.why: Added the diagonal and the two offsets instead of the four boundary lengths: $16 + 8 + 5 = 29\text{ m}$.
Included the internal diagonal in the perimeter: $10 + \sqrt{164} + \sqrt{125} + \sqrt{61} + 16 \approx 57.80\text{ m}$, which rounds to $58\text{ m}$.
Halved the boundary-length sum as though calculating a triangle area: $\frac{10 + \sqrt{164} + \sqrt{125} + \sqrt{61}}{2} \approx 20.90\text{ m}$, which rounds to $21\text{ m}$.

questions.solution_text:
$PQ = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\text{ m}$
$QR = \sqrt{10^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{164}\text{ m}$
$RS = \sqrt{10^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{125}\text{ m}$
$SP = \sqrt{6^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{61}\text{ m}$
$\text{Perimeter} = 10 + \sqrt{164} + \sqrt{125} + \sqrt{61}$
$\approx 41.80\text{ m}$
Rounded to the nearest metre, the perimeter is $42\text{ m}$.

questions.question_text:
An irregular quadrilateral block $ABCD$ has a diagonal $AC = 28\text{ m}$. Both perpendicular offsets meet $AC$ at the same point, $12\text{ m}$ from $A$ and $16\text{ m}$ from $C$. The offsets to $B$ and $D$ are $9\text{ m}$ and $12\text{ m}$ respectively, on opposite sides of $AC$.
What is the perimeter of $ABCD$ to the nearest metre?

options.why: Used twice the diagonal as the perimeter and ignored the offsets: $2 \times 28 = 56\text{ m}$.
Included the internal diagonal in the outer perimeter: $35 + \sqrt{337} + \sqrt{288} + 28 \approx 98.33\text{ m}$, which rounds to $98\text{ m}$.
Used the $9\text{ m}$ offset for both vertices: $2(15 + \sqrt{337}) \approx 66.72\text{ m}$, then incorrectly rounded each $\sqrt{337}$ up to $19\text{ m}$ to obtain $2(15 + 19) = 68\text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A diagonal of an irregular quadrilateral paddock is divided into three consecutive segments of $12.5\text{ m}$, $16.8\text{ m}$ and $9.7\text{ m}$. The perpendicular heights from the opposite vertices to the diagonal are $18.4\text{ m}$ and $23.6\text{ m}$. What is the area to the nearest square metre?

options.why: Omitted the factor of one half: $39 \times (18.4 + 23.6) = 1638\text{ m}^2$.
Omitted the final diagonal segment: $\frac{1}{2} \times (12.5 + 16.8) \times (18.4 + 23.6) = 615.3\text{ m}^2$, which rounds to $615\text{ m}^2$.
Found only the triangle with height $23.6\text{ m}$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 39 \times 23.6 = 460.2\text{ m}^2$, which rounds to $460\text{ m}^2$.

questions.solution_text:
$d = 12.5 + 16.8 + 9.7 = 39\text{ m}$
$A_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 39 \times 18.4 = 358.8\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 39 \times 23.6 = 460.2\text{ m}^2$
$A = A_1 + A_2 = 358.8 + 460.2 = 819\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest square metre, the area is $819\text{ m}^2$.
